items.title: 10 percent of pupils in Grades 1-3 are struggling readers
items.description: Ten percent of Grades 1 to 3 learners are struggling readers, according to the Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM2).

items.title: All senators should reject VP offer – Alan Peter
items.description: Just like impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero, fellow senators should reject any offer from Malacañang to take over the country’s second highest post in case Vice President Sara Duterte is convicted in her impeachment trial, Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano said yesterday.

items.title: ‘Government began preparing for super El Niño last year’
items.description: Contrary to public perception, the Marcos administration began preparing for the effects of the anticipated super El Niño as early as 2025, Social Welfare Secretary Rex Gatchalian said.

items.title: Expanded SOVFAs with like-minded countries eyed
items.description: Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. yesterday raised the possibility of expanding the Philippines’ Status of Visiting Forces Agreements (SOVFAs) with like-minded countries to strengthen international peacekeeping cooperation and enhance military interoperability.

items.title: Ombudsman to monitor budget, review SC ruling
items.description: The Office of the Ombudsman plans to form a group that will review the Supreme Court ruling that struck down the national budgets in 2024 and 2025 along with portions of the 2026 outlay as unconstitutional.

items.title: DepEd: Complete suspension of classes if temperature hits 42 degrees Celsius
items.description: Education Secretary Sonny Angara has issued comprehensive guidelines for schools amid the threat of the super El Niño, ordering the suspension of all physical and home-based academic activities once ambient temperature hits 42 degrees Celsius, to ensure the safety of learners and teachers.

items.title: DFA: No deal with Taiwan on undersea cables
items.description: The Philippines has no special arrangement with Taiwan for the protection of undersea cables or for dealing with Beijing’s “gray zone” activities, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) clarified yesterday, denying a declaration made by Manila’s deputy chief of mission in Washington.

items.title: If Bato doesn’t surrender, what next?
items.description: Efforts to track down Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa would continue if he does not turn himself over to authorities within the one-week deadline set by the police, Malacañang said yesterday.

items.title: DOTr’s Lopez, DPWH’s Dizon swap posts
items.description: President Marcos carried out yet another change in his Cabinet, with Transportation Secretary Giovanni Lopez and Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon swapping posts, in an arrangement supposedly meant to solve commuters’ woes and sustain reforms in a system that “protected” corruption.

items.title: House budget insertions reached P1 trillion – watchdog
items.description: The House-approved version of the P7.2-trillion 2027 national budget contains “red flag” levels of insertions worth over P1 trillion, including around 7,000 infrastructure projects totaling P190 billion, a budget watchdog said.
